Few Things I know already About this Hatchet; it is too heavy, the balance is off, it will shatter, the sheath should have rivets, the head will cut through the stitching, it was "hung" all wrong, brass wedge is a bad idea, I will get blisters, I should only ever use BLO to finish any hatchet, 6061 is the worst aluminum to use for this application, this head will fly off and hurt someone, you can not hold aluminum in the cold, galvanic corrosion will make the hatchet explode in my hand, the leather will slide off and the hatchet will go flying, my arm will vibrate and cause muscle fatigue, the

I chopped this tree down on my property. With lots of tools and muscle I turn it in to 4 identical Country Table legs.. many will ask where is the chainsaw? I can not use the gas chain saw in the city shop and  the electrical chain saw just to dull for precision. I realized this after using for one log. I experimented with various techniques and tools to shape the turning blanks. My best guess on the species of the wood is Hemlock Wood. This tree has been standing dead for 6-8 years, VERY dry. In up coming video ill make table using the legs. Please share like comment and subscribe. follow me

These tables were designed by me and the client.  The design was originally intended to be sapele wood naturally  finished  with a gradual bull nosed (slight rounded) edge, the reason for the thick banding. As the project progress the client wanted the tables to be white washed and more square at the edge.  I tried a brush and hand rub at first but the client wanted the tables to be more white. So I resorted to a spray gloss white enamel finish. 3 coats. Sanding w 400 grit in between coats. 
The grain texture showed through the paint finish The client was happy and so was I.

In this project my bud Rob and I restored and re-assemble this 1890's Cincinnati Drill Press. I recovered this drill press few years ago in an abandon barn. I had to completely dismantle it to move it, and it has sat outside getting very rusty every since. Nearly all  of the rust was removed by Evaporato-Rust for the smaller parts we could soak. The larger parts were cleaned by white wheels and angle grinders! I did need to fabricate few parts in the machine shop, but as you can see this drill press restoration turned out great - Enjoy!

Everyone recognizes those big yellow field goal uprights on game day, but have you ever wondered how they’re made?

Carhartt took my buddy Derek and me to the Sportsfield factory in upstate New York, where we got our hands dirty fabricating, grinding, and powder coating these massive steel structures. Of course, we had to turn it into a competition and see who could do it better. Who did YOU think would win?
